crossing_rule.definition: strict same-physical-height D56 pairwise audit of ALL flat parts merged by z (leads + direct bodies included); exact replica of validate21.check_crossings

header.plane_model: 21 routing heights = 19 body planes + 2 interface-body planes (1001 z=0.0, 1002 z=0.5)

families.definition: Z1_XY = source side X -> target side Y for the 256 Z1-other opposite routes; Z2_XY = source side X -> target side Y for the 400 Z2-other adjacent routes; manual = the 8 frozen U groups

header.forced_class_decision_tree: Classification per crossing pair at its physical height. topology = port_chord_cross: the two routes straight port-to-port chords properly cross (alternating boundary order). (1) forced: both routes are DIRECT interface-body routes on the same interface height. Their entire path is one flat at that height attached to the two boundary ports, so two such flats with alternating ports must intersect on that disk (Jordan curve); the only escape is to convert one route into a 2-transition route (move it off the interface). (2) avoidable: port_chord_cross == false. A crossing-aware 2D router could separate the pair on the SAME height (the baseline layerwise router does no crossing avoidance), so the crossing is a routing-policy artefact. (3) uncertain: port_chord_cross == true for two non-direct routes. Their flat bodies start at interior stub ends (0.25 mm interface lead + R15 S-transition footprint, 2.4-5.1 mm inside the port), so boundary alternation does NOT by itself prove a forced same-height crossing; it shows the pair cannot be separated by an order-preserving 2D fan-out and most likely needs height separation, hence uncertain. separable_by_height = at least one partner is a movable route whose flat at this height is its body (moving that route to another allowed plane removes the same-height contact). A pinned interface lead of a non-direct route can never be moved by re-layering.

verified_against.note: per-plane crossings, crossing pairs, totals and per-route distribution all reproduce the frozen crossing_stats.json

anomaly_L9_L14_Z2_INTERFACE.explanation: All compared planes hold exactly 12 C4 orbits x 4 families = 48 routes, but they hold DIFFERENT orbit blocks of the frozen Z2-other pairing. L9/L14/Z2_INTERFACE carry orbits 233-244 / 221-232 / 209-220, i.e. the 36 "corner-bundle" orbits (E connectors 3-8 x S connectors 9-14): every route is a short 60-90 mm chord that stays inside one board quadrant and the four families live in four disjoint corners, so cross-family chords cannot meet; only the two port rows of the same family interact. L15-L19 carry orbits 129-192, the 64 "grid" orbits (E connectors 1-8 x N connectors 1-8): every route is a 150-220 mm diagonal from one board edge to another, all families share the board centre, 83-86% of all route pairs actually cross and 56-59% of them have alternating ports. The 60 crossings are therefore not a lucky permutation: they are exactly 4 families x 15 staircase crossings of two shifted port rows inside one corner.

Q1.question: Where do the 11890 same-height crossings physically come from?
Q1.answer: Only 13 of the 21 routing heights produce crossings. The 4 manual-U heights L2-L5 and the 4 manual Z2 heights L10-L13 are completely crossing-free and no crossing involves an interface lead. Crossing mass by group: Z1 movable heights (L6,L7,L20,L8,Z1_INTERFACE) = 4510 events (37.9%), the 5 grid Z2 heights (L15-L19) = 7200 events (60.6%), the 3 corner Z2 heights (L9,L14,Z2_INTERFACE) = 180 events (1.5%). Per height: L2(z=-0.35)=0; L3(z=-0.30)=0; L4(z=-0.25)=0; L5(z=-0.20)=0; L6(z=-0.15)=986; L7(z=-0.10)=928; L20(z=-0.05)=964; Z1_INTERFACE(z=+0.00)=896; L8(z=+0.05)=736; L9(z=+0.10)=60; L10(z=+0.15)=0; L11(z=+0.20)=0; L12(z=+0.25)=0; L13(z=+0.30)=0; L14(z=+0.35)=60; L15(z=+0.40)=1246; L16(z=+0.45)=1478; Z2_INTERFACE(z=+0.50)=60; L17(z=+0.55)=1560; L18(z=+0.60)=1476; L19(z=+0.65)=1440.

Q2.question: Which route families / family pairs generate the crossings and what is the per-route distribution?
Q2.answer: All 11890 events belong to movable non-manual routes (manual routes: 0 events, all on the frozen manual heights). 632 of the 656 movable routes are involved, 24 are crossing-free (all on L9/L14/Z2_INTERFACE). Per-route distribution over the 632 involved routes: max 83, p95 60.0, mean 37.63, median 39.0, min 1; over all 1024 routes the mean is 23.22 (392 routes have zero crossings).

Q3.question: Why do L9/L14/Z2_INTERFACE have only 60 crossings when L15/L16/L19 have 1246-1476 with the same 12 orbits x 4 families composition?
Q3.answer: All compared planes hold exactly 12 C4 orbits x 4 families = 48 routes, but they hold DIFFERENT orbit blocks of the frozen Z2-other pairing. L9/L14/Z2_INTERFACE carry orbits 233-244 / 221-232 / 209-220, i.e. the 36 "corner-bundle" orbits (E connectors 3-8 x S connectors 9-14): every route is a short 60-90 mm chord that stays inside one board quadrant and the four families live in four disjoint corners, so cross-family chords cannot meet; only the two port rows of the same family interact. L15-L19 carry orbits 129-192, the 64 "grid" orbits (E connectors 1-8 x N connectors 1-8): every route is a 150-220 mm diagonal from one board edge to another, all families share the board centre, 83-86% of all route pairs actually cross and 56-59% of them have alternating ports. The 60 crossings are therefore not a lucky permutation: they are exactly 4 families x 15 staircase crossings of two shifted port rows inside one corner.

Q4.question: How many crossings are topologically forced, how many are avoidable by 2D re-pathing, and how many need height separation?
Q4.answer: forced=884, avoidable (same-height 2D re-pathing suffices)=3868, uncertain (port chords alternate, so order-preserving 2D separation is impossible and another height is needed)=7138. The forced class is the alternating-port direct-body/direct-body contacts on the two interface heights: 824 events on Z1_INTERFACE and 60 on Z2_INTERFACE. Both routes are then a single flat attached to two boundary ports at that height, so alternating ports make the intersection unavoidable while both stay direct (Jordan curve); the only escape is to convert one route into a 2-transition route. Crossing angle histogram: 15-45deg=665, 45-90deg=10809, 5-15deg=416 (mean 77.33 deg). separable_by_height is true for all 11890 events by the definition (every event has at least one movable body flat), but the binding constraint is topological, not immovability.

Q5.question: Do fan-out / interface leads and lead-space conflicts cause the crossings?
Q5.answer: No. The 460 Z1 + 464 Z2 non-direct routes contribute 1848 fixed 0.25 mm radial interface leads (2 per route) and none of them crosses anything: lead-involved events = 0. Every interface-height event (956) is a direct-body/direct-body contact between the 52 / 48 interface-direct routes. Fan-out pressure is therefore a DENSITY problem on the interface heights (512 route footprints on one height, the most congested height of the stack, min non-crossing centreline 0.105 mm), not a lead-crossing problem.

Q6.question: Which families can share a layer with zero/low crossings, and how should the 256 Z1 / 400 Z2 movable routes be distributed over the allowed planes?
Q6.answer: Plane-sharing risk is the port-chord alternation rate (an alternating pair cannot share a height without a crossing). Z1 group: every vertical x horizontal family pair alternates on 100% of its pairs (Z1_NS x Z1_WE 100%; Z1_EW x Z1_NS 100%; Z1_SN x Z1_WE 100%; Z1_EW x Z1_SN 100%; Z1_EW x Z1_WE 19%; Z1_NS x Z1_SN 19%), while within-family alternation is small (Z1_EW 0.193; Z1_NS 0.191; Z1_SN 0.196; Z1_WE 0.193). Z2 group: the four corner families alternate on ~73% of cross pairs (Z2_EN x Z2_ES 73%; Z2_EN x Z2_NW 73%; Z2_ES x Z2_SW 73%; Z2_NW x Z2_SW 73%), within-family rates Z2_EN 0.204; Z2_ES 0.204; Z2_NW 0.204; Z2_SW 0.204, but the route-level pairing matters more than the family label: the 36 corner-bundle orbits (short chords inside one quadrant) alternate only inside their own family, while the 64 grid orbits (150-220 mm diagonals) alternate with almost everything. Baseline topology conflicts = 7868 pairs. Best computed re-assignment (C_greedy_c4_free) = 724 pairs (C4-free per-route greedy); the C4-orbit-respecting orbit greedy gives 6584 pairs; Z1 vertical/horizontal family separation alone gives 5173 pairs. Recommended distribution: IF the C4-orbit-on-one-plane rule is dropped (that is what the C4-free experiment buys) use the per-route greedy distribution Z1 {6:57,7:57,8:60,1001:60,20:22} and Z2 {9:51,14:51,15:51,16:51,1002:49,17:49,18:49,19:49} - about 105 routes become interface-direct, close to the baseline 100. If the C4 orbits must stay whole the floor stays ~6584, because every orbit mixes vertical and horizontal Z1 routes; the best orbit-respecting fallback is the Z1 vertical/horizontal split plus the Z2 corner/grid split. In both cases keep ~50-60 routes per height and let the crossing-aware 2D router remove the remaining non-alternating events.

strategies.name: B_z1_orientation_split
